home.cap.terminal.title.message: The LibXR terminal runs in the browser

home.cap.terminal.p1.message: The terminal here is LibXR compiled to WebAssembly and running in the browser. `Terminal` provides line editing, history and path completion, and runs the commands stored in `RamFS` by path.

home.cap.terminal.p2.message: On a microcontroller, the same `Terminal` provides a command line over a UART or a USB virtual serial port.

home.cap.terminal.figAlt.message: Line drawing of a terminal window

home.cap.terminal.figCaption.message: The terminal loads the LibXR WebAssembly program in the browser.

home.cap.ring.title.message: UART receive: the hardware keeps writing, software reads on demand

home.cap.ring.p1.message: On microcontrollers the UART driver keeps the receive DMA running. The interrupt works out the new bytes from the DMA write pointer, writes them with `PushBatch` into `SPSCQueue`, the ring queue of the `ReadPort`, and calls `Publish()` to complete pending reads.

home.cap.ring.p2.message: The receive path has no step that stops and restarts the DMA; software only catches up with the hardware write pointer.

home.cap.ring.figAlt.message: Line drawing of DMA writing into a ring queue

home.cap.topic.title.message: Topic: publish and subscribe with an exact type

home.cap.topic.p1.message: `Topic` is an in-process publish/subscribe channel with an exact payload type. A publish is delivered synchronously to the registered subscribers, each of which receives it in one of four ways: synchronous, asynchronous, queued or callback.

home.cap.topic.p2.message: On Linux, `LinuxSharedTopic` keeps the data in shared-memory slots and subscribers read the same memory through descriptors, so no data is copied between processes.

home.cap.topic.doc1.message: Topic Basics, Subscription Models, and Dispatch Semantics

home.cap.topic.figAlt.message: Line drawing of one publisher, four kinds of subscriber and shared-memory slots

home.cap.topic.figCaption.message: Left: a publisher delivers through a Topic to synchronous, asynchronous, queued and callback subscribers. Right: two Linux processes exchange data through shared-memory slots.

home.cap.workflow.title.message: Fetching and locking Modules, generating the main function

home.cap.workflow.p1.message: A BSP lists the Modules it needs in `Modules/modules.yaml`. `xrobot setup` fetches them and locks each one to a commit in `xrobot.lock`, and `xrobot gen` generates the main function `XRobotMain` from a configuration under `User/`.

home.cap.workflow.p2.message: The CI of an STM32 BSP calls a shared workflow: it checks that the generated files match the commit, builds every configuration, and uploads the firmware on a push to `master`, a `v*` tag or a published release.

home.cap.workflow.figAlt.message: Line drawing of Module repositories, the lock, the generated header and the firmware

home.cap.xrusb.title.message: XRUSB: the device-side USB stack and debug interfaces

home.cap.xrusb.p1.message: XRUSB is the USB device stack in LibXR. It provides device classes such as CDC, HID, UAC, GSUSB, CMSIS-DAP v1/v2 and DFU, and one device can contain several device classes at once.

home.cap.xrusb.p2.message: The debug interfaces implement SWD and JTAG with GPIO timing; the DAPLink device classes use them to access a target chip, for example to read the DP `IDCODE`.

home.cap.xrusb.figAlt.message: Line drawing of a host, a debug probe and a target board

home.cap.xrusb.figCaption.message: The host connects over USB to a probe running XRUSB; the probe connects to the target board over SWD.

home.cap.robots.p1.message: The official Source includes Modules for IMUs, magnetometers, barometers, optical flow, laser ranging, grey-scale line following, RC receivers, displays and attitude estimation.

home.cap.robots.p2.message: A configuration selects Modules and fills in their parameters, and `xrobot gen` generates the main function of one robot from it; different configurations make up the firmware of different robots.

showcase.SameCode.lane.loopAria.message: Bare metal has no threads: while waiting, the main loop checks the 1 ms time base and refreshes the timers once per elapsed millisecond; after {ms} refreshes the timer calls BlinkLED.

showcase.topic.aria.message: How one Topic publish reaches each subscriber

showcase.topic.canvas.topic.message: Publisher thread, subscriber list and the four kinds of subscriber

showcase.topic.canvas.shared.message: Publisher process, shared-memory slots and three subscriber processes

showcase.topic.key.label.message: Data copied for subscribers per publish

showcase.topic.key.shared.message: {n} subscribers read the same slot #{k}; each receives a {d} descriptor

showcase.topic.caption.topic.message: One publish walks the subscriber list: a sync subscriber waiting in Wait() is woken with its own copy, an async subscriber gets a copy after StartWaiting(), a queued subscriber gets a copy in its queue, and a callback reads the publisher's data directly.

showcase.topic.caption.shared.message: The publisher writes the data into a shared-memory slot; subscribers receive only the slot number and read the same memory. When every subscriber has released it, the reference count reaches zero and the slot returns to the free queue.

showcase.topic.d.topicNote.message: `LockFreeList::Add` inserts each new subscriber at the head, so the walk starts with the subscriber registered last. During a publish the Topic's busy flag is LOCKED; a default single-publisher Topic runs one publish at a time.

showcase.topic.d.sharedNote.message: The publisher here takes a slot with `CreateData()` and writes into it in place; `Publish(data)` by value first copies the data into the slot once. `PublishData()` sets the reference count to the number of receivers and gives each receiver a `{slot_index, sequence}` descriptor; `Release()` decrements the count, and at 0 the slot returns to the free queue.

showcase.topic.d.config.message: slot_num = {s}, subscriber_num = {u}, queue_num = {q} (the ring holds at most {m} descriptors)

showcase.topic.reduced.message: Reduced motion: the picture stays still; "Publish one" shows the finished delivery.

showcase.ModuleFlow.caption.instance.message: `xrobot instance add` writes the constructor arguments with their defaults; `xrobot instance set` fills each dependency with the name of an object registered in the entry source.
